title: DebianAuthorityManifestV1
description:
The on-disk shape of `policy/debian/authorities.v1.json`.

`pub` so `xtask/src/schemas.rs` can call `schemars::schema_for!(DebianAuthorityManifestV1)` for the §97 schema-snapshot tool. The re-exports in `lib.rs` expose the loader functions, not the struct itself.

PHASE-1.1 PR 1.1.D (policy baseline correctness): the pre-1.1.D struct had a single `baseline_policy_version` field. The spec is explicit (PHASE-1.md line 978) that the `Standards-Version` comparator is the `Standards-Version target` (= `"4.7.4"`), *not* the Policy Manual document version (= `"4.7.4.1"`). The new struct carries both: `policy_document_version` is the document version (for human readers / display), and `standards_version_target` is the comparator the runtime uses. The `Policy`'s `version` in `authorities` is still `4.7.4.1` (the document version the authority *is*).

policy_document_version.description: The version of the Debian Policy *Manual document* (e.g. `"4.7.4.1"`). Display-only — the `Standards-Version` comparator is `standards_version_target`, not this.

standards_version_target.description: The `Standards-Version` target the adapter treats as known good (e.g. `"4.7.4"`). The §22 `delta_review` evaluator compares the candidate's `debian/control` `Standards-Version` against this value.

Authority.description:
A source of policy (§32).

`distribution` is `Some` for distribution-specific authorities (Debian Policy, Fedora Packaging Guidelines) and `None` for cross-distribution authorities (formal specs, generic best practices). The classifier is distribution-neutral; ranking is the adapter's job.

`id` is `#[serde(default)]`-able: a manifest entry that omits `id` deserialises to `AuthorityId::default()` (a nil UUID, per the `define_uuid_id!` macro in `ironmaint-core::identity`). The Debian authority loader (`adapters/debian/src/authority_manifest.rs::load_authorities`) re-mints each loaded entry's id to a fresh UUIDv7 before returning the list, so the runtime id is per-load even though the on-disk default is nil.

AuthorityClassification.description:
Classification of an authority's normative weight (§32).

Adapter-supplied ranking rules apply *over* these labels; the labels themselves are distribution-neutral.

oneOf.description: Binding distribution policy (e.g. Debian Policy, Fedora Packaging Guidelines).
Industry best practice (not binding on the distribution).
Tool documentation (lintian, rpmlint, sbuild, mock, etc.).
Informational — does not assert any obligation.
